messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.content:
**Standard error (standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean)**  

For a one‑sample t‑test the denominator of the test statistic is the *standard error* (SE) of the sample mean:

\[
\text{SE} = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}
\]

where  
- \(s = 1.4\) (sample standard deviation)  
- \(n = 40\) (sample size)

\[
\text{SE} = \frac{1.4}{\sqrt{40}} \approx \frac{1.4}{6.3249} \approx 0.2213
\]

So the standard deviation of the null‑hypothesis test (i.e., the standard error of the mean under the null) is **≈ 0.22**.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6."

They want the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test? That likely refers to the standard error of the mean under null hypothesis? The standard error = sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). But they mention population mean 98.6. For a one-sample t-test, the test statistic is (sample_mean - population_mean) / (sample_std_dev / sqrt(n)). The denominator is the standard error. So compute SE = 1.4 / sqrt(40). sqrt(40) ≈ 6.3249. 1.4 / 6.3249 ≈ 0.2213. So standard deviation of the null hypothesis test (i.e., standard error) is about 0.2213.

Alternatively, maybe they want the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under null: same as SE. So answer: ~0.221.

We can also compute p-value? But they didn't ask. They asked to calculate standard deviation of null hypothesis test. So answer: 0.2213.
